current.text: He played about two-thirds of last season without Trae Young or CJ McCollum. After McCollum arrived, his assists fell by about one per game, his time on the ball, steals, blocks and shooting efficiency dropped, and he was not a top 30 player.
His shooting efficiency and defensive stats dropped late last season and in the playoffs.
Experts think he wore down late last season after a big jump in minutes and a heavier offensive load.

He is a projected starter at power forward next to McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Daniels and Okongwu, with 30-plus minutes expected. Atlanta has no true point guard, and ball handling is shared among McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Johnson and Daniels.
Power forward depth behind him is bad to start the season.
Sharing creation with McCollum for a full season should cut his assists, usage, steals and shooting a bit. Experts expect it to be hard for him to repeat last season's numbers.
Experts say he is not a first-round player in category leagues and that ranks and ADPs around picks 6 to 10 are too high. Lloyd would take him in the middle of round two.
In points leagues, experts consider him a fair pick around picks 8 to 12 and a first-round player.
In a 2026-10-05 auction mock draft he went for 33 USD, less than Josh expected.
Atlanta's fantasy playoff schedule is 4-4-3 games in weeks 19 to 21. The team has 14 back-to-backs, and resting players is not expected to be a concern.
Atlanta is projected to win about 46 games and finish between fourth and eighth in the East.

durable.text: He is excellent in points, rebounds and assists, and he is a strong playmaker for a forward. His rebounds and assists are league outliers.
Experts call his percentages and his three-point shooting iffy.
He commits many turnovers, a clear weakness against the league.
He was injured in every season before last season. Last season was his first healthy year.

Experts disagree on his injury risk. Lloyd calls his past wrist and shoulder injuries fluky and is not concerned. Others call his medical history checkered and say calling him reliable after one healthy season is premature.

note: Experts agree that his market price (Yahoo average cost 51.4 USD, ESPN 53.9 USD, ranks 11 and 9) is too high for category leagues. He went for 34 USD in our league last season and for 33 USD in a recent mock, so aim for the mid 30s to low 40s USD rather than first-round money. His rebounds and assists are elite for a forward, but he averages about 3.3 turnovers, so he fits punt TO builds best. Early in the season, check his assists, steals and FG% with McCollum on the floor, since they fell after McCollum arrived last season.
